rules.rationale: This is the terminating base equation for the named outputOK proof predicate: once the current index is past N, an empty remaining sequence satisfies the summary.
This is the even-index recurrence defining outputOK: it consumes the factorial-valued head and advances both accumulators and the index.
This is the odd-index recurrence defining outputOK: it consumes the triangular-sum-valued head and advances both accumulators and the index.

This simplification adds associativity of ValSeq concatenation, an algebraic fact about the pre-existing valSeqConcat operation that is assumed by the verification module and is not separately proved in Stage 1.

This simplification adds the right-identity law for the pre-existing valSeqConcat operation; the reference definition only computes structurally from the left, and Stage 1 supplies this additional algebraic fact without a prior exact proof.

This simplification assumes left cancellation of a common ValSeq prefix under equality, an additional mathematical property used to expose the existential suffix and not an operational rule or separately proved Stage 1 theorem.

This simplification assumes that a finite sequence equal to itself concatenated with a suffix forces that suffix to be empty; Stage 1 trusts this cancellation consequence rather than proving the exact rule first.
